subject: COBOL words
notes: kb/Work PB661 (w1095g). The row carries three sentences of §8.3.2.2, each re-checked: (1) `OK §8.3.2.2 2)` "When call-convention-name-1 is specified in an applicable CALL-CONVENTION compiler directive, that method-name is treated as a literal that maps, in a manner defined by the implementor" - no subject: WiseOwl COBOL defines no call-convention-name (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-68, which now states the INVOKE arms too), and since kb/Work PB1383 any other word is COBOL1911; re-probed on the w1095g build: `>>CALL-CONVENTION STDCALL` + universal INVOKE -> COBOL1911 at 2002, 2014 and 2023 (conformance:cases/7.3.9-CALL-CONVENTION/pb1383-call-convention-undefined-name). This is the INVOKE twin of GR-8.3.2.2-L5.2 b) and is closed on the same ground. (2) `OK §8.3.2.2 2)` "the naming convention and mapping to be used for the method-name is determined by the entry convention of the class or interface that contains the method" - the only entry convention is COBOL (ENTRY-CONVENTION IS <other> is COBOL2385, DOC-A.1-64), whose mapping is §8.3.2.2's (`OK §11.9.7.4 2)` "When COBOL is specified, the naming convention and mapping of method-names and program-names are as specified in 8.3.2.2"): a typed INVOKE T "MIXEDEXT" on a class stating ENTRY-CONVENTION IS COBOL reaches METHOD-ID M2 AS "MixedExt" (conformance:cases/8.3.2.2-User-defined-words/w1095g_pb661_entry_convention_invoke_mapping), and stated or inherited COBOL conventions on classes and interfaces map "sayhi" to SayHi (conformance:cases/8.3.2.2-User-defined-words/l1c06_entry_convention_oo); the AS arm is also pinned by conformance:cases/8.3.2.2-User-defined-words/pb303_as_module_name_and_invoke. (3) `OK §8.3.2.2 2)` "the ENTRY-CONVENTION, if any, in the class or interface definition containing the method is ignored" - a universal INVOKE U "mixedext" on the same ENTRY-CONVENTION IS COBOL class reaches M2 by the COBOL call convention's word mapping (GR-8.3.2.2-L4.1, OoMethodSymbol.DispatchKey) and U "M2" (the declared word) sets EC-OO-METHOD; under one convention honouring and ignoring the clause give one answer, so the golden pins the mapping the sentence leaves, not the ignoring itself. The docs/CONFORMANCE.md self-contradiction the w67q extension named (items 13, 16, 19 and 141 said there is no CALL-CONVENTION directive, or that every name is processed as a COBOL name) is corrected to the PB1383 state: the directive admits only COBOL.
